_comment: Copy this file to watch-config.json and edit. watch-config.json is never committed.
_cloud_cidrs: Optional. IP ranges are a FALLBACK only: they decide a destination's nature when no hostname could be resolved. Domain/SNI markers do the real work, so a handful of ranges here is usually enough.
_cloud_cidr_files: Optional. Extra files holding large CIDR lists, so a multi-thousand-range list does not turn this file into an unreadable wall. Each file is either ["1.2.3.0/24", ...] or {"cidrs": [...]}. Ranges are merged at load and looked up by binary search, so tens of thousands of entries stay cheap.
_marker_groups: Groups of domain markers. A 'suspicious: true' group is treated as possible exfiltration destinations and lands in watch-candidates.txt / watch-blockable.txt. A 'suspicious: false' group is labelled only: it gets its own section in the report and never enters the block list. A hostname is classified by its LONGEST matching marker, so a specific ad marker beats a broad provider marker. Backwards compatible: a flat "cloud_domain_markers": ["a.com", ...] behaves like one suspicious group.
_service_kinds: Optional. [[substring, label]] pairs that name a destination you already recognise. Checked before the generic storage / log / CDN keyword heuristics.
